task: With RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER set, sccache fails with "Compiler not supported" as soon as cargo starts, but exporting CARGO=$(which cargo) by hand makes it work. Has this been seen before, what causes it, and where was it fixed?
gold: The rustc -vV version probe goes through RUSTC_WRAPPER / RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER, but cargo did not set the CARGO environment variable for that probe (unlike normal compilations, which get it via Compilation::fill_env)
sccache relies on CARGO to detect the workspace-wrapper pattern, so without it it reports the compiler as unsupported
The fix sets CARGO (cmd.env(CARGO_ENV, gctx.cargo_exe())) before the -vV invocation in Rustc::new in the rustc.rs util module

task: After touching a file that a build script watches via rerun-if-changed, `cargo check` re-checks the crate on every single run and never becomes fresh again, even though nothing changes. Why, and what was done about it?
gold: Since rustc 1.90 (rust-lang/rust#114669) incremental compilation skips regenerating .rmeta when nothing changed, so the crate's .rmeta keeps an older mtime than the re-run build script execution
Cargo's mtime-based freshness then sees the build script output as newer than the .rmeta and re-checks forever (a no-op check that never updates the file)
The workaround force-updates the mtime of the check-mode outputs (.rmeta) after rustc finishes, in the rustc() function of the compiler module (only for mode.is_check())

task: A Windows user with a `cargo:token-from-stdout` credential helper gets "failed to parse header value" when talking to their alternative registry, and they cannot send any request. Known issue? Cause and fix?
gold: The helper prints the token terminated by \r\n; the adaptor only stripped \n, leaving a trailing \r in the token
Since the 1.96 registry network refactor the request is built with http::HeaderValue, which rejects the trailing \r, producing 'failed to parse header value'
Fix: after trimming \n, also strip a trailing \r in the credential adaptor (BasicProcessCredential in credential/adaptor.rs)

task: CI jobs that run several cargo commands concurrently sometimes hang forever (killed after six hours) waiting on the package cache lock. Has a cause like this been found before, and what was the fix?
gold: In CacheState::lock with MutateExclusive, the mutate_lock is acquired first, then the cache_lock; if the second would block, it returned WouldBlock without releasing mutate_lock
Only the error path and CacheLock::drop decrement mutate_lock, and try_lock creates a CacheLock only on LockAcquired, so the mutate lock stayed held and later lockers deadlocked
Fix: call self.mutate_lock.decrement() before returning WouldBlock (in cache_lock.rs)

task: I'd like to add a `frame-pointers` option to Cargo profiles, with values including a force-off setting. Has this been tried, and is there any reason not to?
gold: A frame-pointers profile option was added (#16742) and then reverted (#16999)
The concern was that the force-off value is confusing: it does not force frame pointers off, it only turns off the force-on option
Force-off is already the default and the actual behaviour can change per target

task: The unused-dependencies lint has false positives. Should we give users an ignore list / allowlist in the manifest so they can silence specific dependencies?
gold: An unused deps ignore list was added and then reverted
Instead, cargo ignores unused direct dependencies that are also transitive dependencies (they are still used somewhere), which removes the false positives without an allowlist
Remaining cases like curl, whose build.rs dynamically picks dependencies, were judged an exception not worth direct support; the allowlist question was punted pending rust-lang/rfcs#3920

task: Users want `cargo install` to honour `resolver.lockfile-path` from their config so they can point it at a lockfile. Should it?
gold: No: cargo install was changed to ignore resolver.lockfile-path
The [resolver] config table was designed to not apply to cargo install (it overrides resolution for local development only)
This reverted earlier behaviour where cargo install used the configured lockfile path and required it to exist

task: On a Mac whose target directory lives on a ZFS volume, uplifting build artifacts sometimes fails or stalls with EAGAIN (os error 35) when cargo copies a file. Does cargo handle this?
gold: Yes: on macOS cargo copies (fs::copy, clonefile) instead of hard-linking; if the copy fails with EAGAIN (35) it falls back to fs::hard_link
Retrying the copy could take a long time (up to about 4 seconds) while hard-linking works immediately; it is likely the OpenZFS-on-OSX bug openzfsonosx/zfs#809 (cargo issue #13838)
The workaround lives in _link_or_copy in crates/cargo-util/src/paths.rs

task: On FreeBSD, cargo fails to fetch the crates.io index with "[60] SSL peer certificate or SSH remote key was not OK (... unable to get local issuer certificate (20))". What is going on, and how has cargo dealt with it?
gold: It was caused by curl-sys 0.4.84, which broke certificate validation on FreeBSD 13.5/14.3 (notably clean installs without the ca_root_nss package), issue #16357
Cargo downgraded curl-sys to 0.4.83 (and had to re-downgrade later when it was bumped again)
It was later bumped to 0.4.86, deliberately skipping 0.4.84, since the problem only occurs on 0.4.84 (alexcrichton/curl-rust#632)

task: When a registry download hits a spurious network error, how many times does cargo retry by default, how long does it wait between attempts, and does it respect a server's Retry-After header?
gold: Default is 3 retries (MAX_RETRY_DEFAULT), configurable with net.retry
First retry waits 500 ms plus a random 0-1000 ms jitter; later retries wait (retries-1)*3 s + 500 ms, capped at 10 s
A Retry-After value from the server is used when present, capped at the 10 s maximum sleep
